page: Microsoft Azure DC2es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on Intel Xeon TDX silicon running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via multithreading, clocked at up to 4.2 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation. Its cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage, requiring external block volumes, and includes no GPU accelerators.

Performance testing indicates a divergence between single-threaded efficiency and aggregate multi-core throughput. Bolstered by its 4.2 GHz clock speed, Geekbench single-core testing reached 1996.0 points, placing the VM in the top quartile of evaluated systems. The underlying processor provides advanced instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. In contrast, parallel capabilities remain constrained by the single physical core. Geekbench multi-core performance registered 2401.0 points and stress-ng multi-core testing scored 1939.61, both residing in lower benchmark percentiles. Throughput-dependent tasks like Clang code compilation and PassMark physics tests similarly demonstrate entry-level performance bounds.

From an efficiency perspective, the DC2es_v6 offers access to modern Intel Xeon compute features without the overhead of larger multi-core footprints. While it lacks the concurrent processing capability required for high-volume database engines or large-scale data caches, it provides consistent execution for serial workloads. This server profile is appropriately sized for lightweight web services, isolated utility routines, low-traffic APIs, and development environments that rely on high per-core speeds without heavy multithreading requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure DC2es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance equipped with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon TDX processor operating at up to 4.2 GHz. Supported by 8.0 GB of memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization with dedicated CPU allocation. The underlying Intel architecture provides broad instruction support, including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography flags like AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-thread capability, registering top-quartile Geekbench single-core performance. Conversely, multi-core throughput and memory-bound metrics reflect its compact dual-thread footprint, ranking in lower performance quartiles for parallel compilation, physics calculations, and Redis operations. The DC2es_v6 serves as a cost-efficient entry-level compute target suited for lightweight web services, small microservices, and modest background utility tasks requiring high per-core execution speeds.
